title: White rice with tomatoes and/or tomato-based sauce, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: This is boiled white rice prepared with tomatoes or a tomato‑based sauce without any added fat. Rice provides complex carbohydrates, while tomatoes add flavor, aroma, and valuable nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is one of the most widely consumed grains worldwide.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their bright red color.
Cooking rice without fat keeps its caloric density low, making it diet‑friendly.
Fat‑free tomato sauce is often made from tomato puree, water, and spices.
The rice‑tomato combination is common in Mediterranean and Asian traditional dishes.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of glucose needed for brain and muscle function.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes contain vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Tomatoes are a good source of potassium, important for fluid balance.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Even fat‑free tomato sauce may contain salt; people limiting sodium should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, mixed with tomato sauce or fresh chopped tomatoes. Add herbs, spices, or a splash of lemon juice to enhance flavor. It works well as a side dish for meat, fish, or vegetable meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Keep the tomato sauce separate, also refrigerated, for up to 5 days. Reheat thoroughly to at least 75 °C before serving.
